{\Large\bfseries Decision record}\par\smallskip
\textbf{Project title:} Landmarks of the Wikipedia game: are the pages players aim for the best hubs?\\
\textbf{Members:} Raphaël Hazan, Nicolas Salapete, Edouard Souied, Josh Soussan\\
\textbf{Repository:} \url{https://github.com/joshsssn/DDS_final_project}
(report: \texttt{report/report.pdf}; full decision log: \texttt{docs/decisions.md})

\section*{Part 1. Decisions}

\stage{Collection}
{Official Wikimedia SQL dumps of French Wikipedia, pinned to \DumpDate{} (most recent complete
dump), five tables (\RawGB\,GB). \texttt{download.py} streams them with resume support and checks
each file against the official SHA-1 sums; our own streaming parser reads each file's
\texttt{CREATE TABLE} statement. Small secondary collection: the rendered HTML of \BiasNPages{}
pages through the MediaWiki API, to measure template links.}
{Crawling pages through the API: weeks for \NArticles{} articles, revisions from different
dates, load on Wikimedia servers. Importing the dumps into MySQL: a server to install for a
one-off read.}
{The graph is one dated snapshot. It keeps template links, which are clickable but inflate
degrees; the dumps do not say which links come from templates. Old dumps leave the main server
(mirrors documented in the README).}
{\texttt{docs/provenance.md}, \texttt{docs/source\_justification.md}, report §2. The parser
keeps all \NLinkRows{} \texttt{pagelinks} rows, the same totals as an independent
\texttt{zcat | grep -c} count (\texttt{data/interim/independent\_row\_counts.txt}).}

\stage{Cleaning}
{Measure first, then transform. Keep namespace-0 articles; resolve link targets that are
redirects to their final article (\NLinksViaRedirect{} links, \ShareLinksViaRedirect); drop red
links (\ShareRedLinks), links to other namespaces (\ShareLinksOtherNs), self-loops and duplicates.
Disambiguation pages stay traversable but are never start or target.}
{Dropping links to redirects removes real paths; keeping redirects as nodes adds a fake click.
Removing template links would need every page's wikitext, i.e.\ another source.}
{Hub quality depends only on this graph. We checked that redirect resolution does not drive the
ranking: for the 20 best hubs, a median \RedirTopMedShare{} of the in-degree comes only through
redirects (at most \RedirTopMaxShare).}
{\texttt{docs/data\_quality.md}, \texttt{data/processed/quality.json}, report Table~1,
\texttt{redirect\_share.json}.}

\stage{Storage}
{A compressed sparse row (CSR) adjacency in NumPy arrays (forward and reverse,
\CsrDiskGB\,GB) plus a Parquet node table, memory-mapped. Our workload is full BFS on a static,
read-only graph.}
{DuckDB with an edge table, benchmarked on the same queries: one forward BFS takes \DuckBfsS\,s
against \CsrBfsS\,s (\DuckBfsRatio$\times$ slower), a reverse BFS \DuckRevBfsRatio$\times$ slower.
Neo4j discussed only: a server and an import of \NEdges{} relationships for no gain on full
traversals.}
{Fast BFS (about \NBfsRuns{} runs in the project) but no ad-hoc queries on the CSR, and any
cleaning change means rebuilding it. DuckDB is kept where it fits: the joins of the cleaning step.}
{\texttt{docs/storage.md} (detailed comparison), report §4 and Table~2,
\texttt{storage\_benchmark.json}.}

\stage{Analysis}
{Exact BFS distances. For \NPairs{} random pairs (seed \Seed) and \NCandidates{} candidate hubs,
the mean detour $d(s,h)+d(h,t)-d(s,t)$ and the share of pairs where $h$ lies on a shortest path.
Candidates come from four lists (top-\TopK{} by out-degree, by in-degree, by frequency on sampled
shortest paths, and \NRandomBaseline{} random articles). Perceived and real criteria are compared
with Spearman's $\rho$ inside each list and a top-\TopOverlapK{} overlap.}
{Evaluating every article as a hub (two BFS for each of \NEligible{} articles: months of computation), or
candidates from out-degree only, which would make the comparison circular.}
{Results hold only among the candidates; a better hub outside them cannot be excluded. An
independent sample (seed \OtherSeed) gives the same 15 best hubs \SeedTopFifteenOrder{}
($\rho=\SeedRho$).}
{\texttt{reports/generated/sample\_seed42\_n200000/} (\texttt{results.json}, \texttt{hubs.csv}), report §5–6.}

\stage{Communication}
{Main figure: out-degree (the perceived criterion) against mean detour (the real one), one point
per candidate, coloured by the list it comes from (report Fig.~1a). The two axes put the question
in one picture: lists sit at the far right with large detours, \BestHub{} at the bottom.}
{A single pooled correlation coefficient, or a table of the best hubs alone: neither shows that
the link-richest pages are lists, nor how the four lists differ.}
{The groups overlap on a log axis, so the title gives $\rho$ inside each list. Each number in the
report and slides is a LaTeX macro written by the code (\texttt{report\_numbers.py}).}
{Report Fig.~1, \texttt{src/wikigame/figures.py}, slides 10--12.}

\section*{Part 2. Response to feedback}

\subsection*{Round 1 (review of the proposal)}
The implementation already answered most of these points; the labelling protocol was added to the
report after the review.
\begin{itemize}
\fb{Candidates taken from out-degree make the comparison circular.}{Candidates come from four
lists: top-\TopK{} by out-degree, in-degree and path frequency, plus \NRandomBaseline{} random
articles.}{Report §5.}
\fb{Number of pairs, candidate set and statistic not given.}{\NPairs{} pairs, \TopK{} per list,
Spearman's $\rho$ and top-\TopOverlapK{} overlap, all in \texttt{config.yaml}.}{Report §5.}
\fb{What happens to pairs without a path?}{Counted and reported separately, never dropped:
\NUnreachable{} pairs (\ShareUnreachable).}{Report §6.}
\fb{How will the template-link bias be measured?}{Rendered HTML of \BiasNPages{} pages through the
API, with and without navigation boxes.}{Report Fig.~1d, \texttt{bias\_check.py}.}
\fb{Labelling protocol missing.}{\NTypeLabels{} types fixed in advance, labels from page titles,
one full re-reading.}{Report §5, \texttt{docs/decisions.md} §15.}
\fb{Not acted on: a survey of players, and the English Wikipedia.}{A survey is a new dataset and
answers another question (what players believe); the English edition is outside our scope. Both
appear as limits.}{\texttt{docs/decisions.md} §27, report §7.}
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Round 2 (review of the intermediate version)}
\begin{itemize}
\fb{The pooled $\rho$ between out-degree and detour depends on how candidates were selected.}{We
report $\rho$ inside each list: \RhoOutDetourInGrpOut{} among the top out-degree pages, negative
in the three others.}{Report §6, Fig.~1a.}
\fb{Templates inflate in-degree too.}{We give the in-degree correlation without the
\NReferenceCandidates{} reference pages: $\rho=\RhoInDetour$ becomes $\RhoInDetourNoRef$.}{Report §6.}
\fb{Redirect resolution may favour countries.}{Measured: it does not change the ranking (see
Cleaning).}{\texttt{redirect\_share.py}, \texttt{docs/decisions.md} §28.}\fb{Small types are ranked (\TypeContinentN{} continents ranked first).}{Types with fewer than \MinTypeSize{}
pages are merged and not ranked.}{Fig.~1c, \texttt{config.yaml}.}
\fb{\texttt{run.py figures} fails on a fresh copy; \texttt{docs/} was not on GitHub.}{Figures
read a small versioned file of degree counts; \texttt{docs/} is versioned.}{README.}
\fb{\texttt{pairs.csv} stores unreachable pairs as 255; labels can be missing silently.}{Empty
value, page ids added, data dictionary in the README; the code warns about a missing label.}
{\texttt{docs/decisions.md} §15, §21.}
\fb{Not acted on: the RAM and network limits of the reviewers' machine.}{The full pipeline needs
the dumps and $\geq$16\,GB of RAM; figures and report numbers can be regenerated without
them.}{README.}
\end{itemize}
